objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 67-year-old woman with a change in mental status and abdominal discomfort.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve been more confused lately and I can’t really put what I’m feeling into words. I also feel uncomfortable when you press on my right upper abdomen, and I’ve had a fever around 102°F.
Doctor: When did you first notice the confusion and the right‑upper‑abdominal discomfort, and how have those symptoms changed over time

Patient: The confusion started a few days ago and has been getting worse, and the discomfort on the right upper side has been present since around the same time. The fever came on more recently, and I’ve felt generally unwell overall with no clear periods of improvement.
Doctor: Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or changes in the color of your stool or urine?

Patient: I’ve had less appetite and I feel quite nauseated at times, but I haven’t been vomiting much. I’m not sure about my stool or urine color because I’ve been too confused to notice and my care staff hasn’t told me of any changes.
Doctor: Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or pale stools that might suggest jaundice?

Patient: I’m not able to tell if my skin or eyes are yellow, and I don’t know about dark urine or pale stools because I can’t reliably check, though I feel worse overall. My staff hasn’t mentioned any color changes to me.
Doctor: Can you describe the pain in your right upper abdomen—its intensity, quality (sharp, dull, cramping), whether it radiates anywhere, and if anything makes it better or worse?

It feels like a tender, uncomfortable ache right under my right ribs, and it seems to get worse when you press on it. It doesn’t really spread anywhere that I can tell, and I’m not sure what makes it better since I’ve just been feeling generally unwell.
Doctor: Have you had any recent illnesses, surgeries, hospitalizations, or procedures (such as endoscopy, catheter placement, or IV drug use) in the past few weeks?

Patient: No recent surgeries or procedures that I know of, and I haven’t had any new hospital stays in the last few weeks. I’m currently in home hospice care, and I don’t recall any recent illness before the confusion and the right upper abdominal discomfort started.
Doctor: Are you taking any medications right now (including pain relievers, antibiotics, sedatives, or hospice‑related drugs), and have any doses been changed recently?

Patient: I’m on hospice medications, but I can’t list all the names or doses—some were adjusted around the time this confusion started. I haven’t noticed any new medication introductions, though I’m not sure what changed in the last few days.
Doctor: Have you had any cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, or sputum production that might suggest a lung infection?

Patient: I haven’t really had a cough or any noticeable trouble breathing, and I don’t think I’ve had chest pain or sputum. Most of what I notice is the worsening confusion, the fever, and the discomfort in my right upper abdomen.
Doctor

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few more things—have you had any shaking chills, sweating, or new severe weakness? Also, do you notice any worsening sleepiness, trouble staying awake, or new problems following simple instructions?

Patient: I’ve had a few shaking chills, especially at night, and I’ve been sweating a lot when the fever spikes. I feel much weaker than usual—I can’t get up from the chair without help. I’ve also been getting drowsier; it’s harder to stay awake, and I’ve been mixing up simple instructions that I used to follow without trouble

Patient: Yes, I’ve had shaking chills at night and then heavy sweating when the fever rises. I feel much weaker than usual and I’m getting drowsier, having trouble staying awake and I can’t follow simple instructions like I could before.
Doctor

Doctor: Thank you. On a scale of 0–10, how bad is the right-upper-abdominal discomfort, and do you feel any worsening after meals? Also, have you noticed whether you’re more confused at certain times of day or after taking your hospice medicines?
Doctor: Do you have any known liver or gallbladder problems (such as cirrhosis, gallstones, or a history of biliary disease) or a diagnosis of cancer that involves the abdomen?

Doctor: Do you have any known liver or gallbladder problems (such as cirrhosis, gallstones, or a history of biliary disease) or a diagnosis of cancer that involves the abdomen? Patient: I’m not sure of the exact diagnoses from before hospice, but I’ve been told at some point that there were serious problems involving my health overall; I don’t remember specifically about my liver or gallbladder. I also can’t confirm any abdominal cancer history because my care team hasn’t gone into details with me.
Doctor: Have you had any recent urinary symptoms—such as burning when you urinate, increased frequency, urgency, or any foul‑smelling urine—that might suggest a urinary tract infection?
Patient: I don’t really notice burning or urgency, but my confusion makes it hard to tell. My staff hasn’t mentioned any foul-smelling urine or new urinary problems to me.
Doctor: Do you have a known diagnosis of cancer, and if so, what type and where is it located?

Patient: I don’t know of any specific cancer diagnosis I can name, and I haven’t been told details about where it might be—only that I’m in hospice because of serious illness. I can’t recall whether my liver or gallbladder was ever specifically mentioned to me.
Doctor: Have you or the staff noticed any yellowing of your eyes (scleral icterus) or skin that might indicate jaundice?

Patient: I don’t think so, but I’m not confident—I can’t really look in the mirror, and my staff hasn’t told me that my eyes or skin look yellow. I just know I’ve been getting more confused, I’ve had a fever around 102°F, and it’s tender in my right upper abdomen.
[DDX] Acute cholangitis, Hepatic abscess, Acute cholecystitis, Sepsis of unknown source (e.g., urinary or pulmonary), Hepatic encephalopathy secondary to liver failure
